Among 24 preselected isolates representing four Morchella species, M. sextelata Mel-21 obtained the highest composite screening score under 1 mol·L-1 NaCl and was selected for detailed analysis. A concentration of 300 mmol·L-1 NaCl was subsequently selected as the representative stress condition. Salt stress increased electrical conductivity, osmotic pressure, Na+ accumulation, antioxidant enzyme activities, and proline content, while decreasing the K+/Na+ and Ca2+/Na+ ratios. Intracellular and extracellular polysaccharides showed distinct time-dependent accumulation patterns, and the corresponding crude extracts exhibited increased radical-scavenging activities under NaCl stress. Relative to the common 0 h baseline, RNA-seq identified 3654, 3843, 4289, 3566, and 2494 differentially expressed genes after 3, 6, 12, 24, and 48 h of NaCl exposure, respectively. These genes were enriched in pathways related to ribosomes, oxidative phosphorylation, protein processing in the endoplasmic reticulum, carbohydrate metabolism, and ABC transporters. Gene05935, encoding a predicted multi-pass transmembrane protein, showed consistently higher transcript abundance during NaCl exposure than at the common 0 h baseline. Heterologous expression of Gene05935 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae was associated with higher mean endpoint OD600 values under the tested high-salinity conditions, while the Arabidopsis thaliana assay provided preliminary qualitative observations of seedling appearance during NaCl exposure. Because time-matched untreated controls were not included, the transcriptomic differences cannot be attributed specifically to NaCl. Together, the physiological measurements and temporal expression profiles identify Gene05935 as a candidate for further functional characterization and may inform future cultivation-oriented evaluation of Morchella under saline conditions.

title: ACTL7A Expression and Functional Characteristics of Sperm in Infertile Men: A Comparison Between High and Low DNA Damage Groups, A Cross Sectional Study.
abstract: Male infertility accounts for nearly half of all infertility cases, worldwide, and is frequently associated with molecular abnormalities that cannot be detected by routine semen analysis. Actin-like protein 7A (ACTL7A), a testis-specific actin-related protein essential for spermatogenesis, acrosome integrity, and oocyte activation, has recently emerged as a potential regulator of sperm function. This study aimed to investigate the association between ACTL7A expression and sperm DNA integrity in infertile men. In this comparative cross-sectional study, sixty men were divided into two groups based on sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI), measured by the sperm chromatin structure assay (SCSA): low DFI (<20%) and high DFI (>20%). Semen parameters, chromatin integrity (aniline blue, chromomycin A3, toluidine blue), and oxidative stress markers [dihydroethidium (DHE) fluorescence and total antioxidant capacity (TAC)], were evaluated. The expression level of ACTL7A was quantified by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) and Western blot, and its subcellular localization was determined by immunofluorescence microscopy. Men with high DFI exhibited significantly reduced sperm motility, elevated levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and markedly compromised sperm chromatin integrity, accompanied by decreased ACTL7A expression (P=0.013). No significant differences in sperm morphology or TAC were observed between the groups. Immunofluorescence localized ACTL7A to the equatorial and acrosomal regions of the sperm head. Notably, ACTL7A protein levels correlated strongly with progressive motility (r=0.82, P=0.012). Consistently, individuals with high sperm DNA damage displayed a pronounced reduction in ACTL7A expression, with RNA levels decreased by ~3.4-fold and protein levels by ~2.2-fold, compared to those with low DNA damage. ACTL7A may serve as a potential indicator of sperm DNA integrity and motility, warranting further validation as a biomarker.

title: Integrative Genetic, Transcriptomic, and Single-Cell Analyses Prioritize Druggable Candidate Genes in Knee Osteoarthritis.
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common degenerative joint disease with a complex pathogenesis and a lack of effective molecular targets. This study aimed to prioritize druggable genes associated with KOA and investigate their expression patterns and cellular localization by integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and single-cell analyses. We first screened for potential druggable genes genetically associated with KOA using MR analysis. Subsequently, batch-corrected synovial transcriptomic data were analyzed using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and the genes of the most relevant module were integrated with the MR candidates. A total of 127 machine-learning pipelines were evaluated using repeated nested cross-validation, followed by external validation and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretation. The expression levels of key genes were further validated by experiments. Single-cell RNA sequencing, immune-cell deconvolution, and peripheral immune-cell-specific eQTL-MR were used to investigate the cellular contexts potentially associated with the candidate genes. Finally, potential drug-gene interactions were retrieved from DGIdb, and selected target-compound pairs were evaluated using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. A total of 315 druggable genes showed nominal MR associations with KOA. After integrating KOA-associated WGCNA module, we identified 15 candidate genes. Next, the random forest was selected as the optimal machine-learning model, achieving a mean outer-cross-validation AUC of 0.929 (95% CI, 0.913-0.945). SHAP and differential-expression analyses prioritized four genes. JUN, ADAMTS1, and CRISPLD2 were downregulated in KOA synovium, whereas CX3CR1 was upregulated, and these expression patterns were supported by experimental validation. Single-cell analysis revealed that JUN, ADAMTS1, and CRISPLD2 were predominantly expressed in fibroblast-related populations and CX3CR1 was mainly expressed in myeloid cells, with their expression varying across fibroblast and macrophage states. Peripheral immune-cell-specific eQTL-MR identified nominal associations for JUN in plasma cells, ADAMTS1 in NK_R cells, and CX3CR1 in NK cells. However, none remained significant after correction for multiple testing. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations showed that the ADAMTS1-pravastatin and CX3CR1-Rugocrixan complexes maintained stable protein-ligand contacts during their respective simulations. Integrative multi-omics analyses identified JUN, ADAMTS1, CRISPLD2, and CX3CR1 as prioritized candidate genes associated with KOA. These genes were associated with distinct states of synovial fibroblasts and myeloid cells. These findings provide a foundation for further mechanistic validation and experimental evaluation of candidate drug-target interactions.

title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with virtual knockout analysis identifies FOS as an epithelial-associated candidate gene in chronic atrophic gastritis.
abstract: Chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) is a precancerous lesion characterized by epithelial injury, glandular atrophy, and impaired gastric function. Molecular targets linking epithelial alterations with potential traditional Chinese medicine-derived compounds remain unclear. GEO bulk transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), which were intersected with CAG-related genes for enrichment analysis. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis and reverse network pharmacology were used to identify key targets and construct a drug-component-target network. Single-cell RNA sequencing, virtual knockout, molecular docking, CCK-8 assay, and RT-qPCR in 1‑Methyl‑3‑nitro‑1‑nitrosoguanidine (MNNG)-treated GES-1 cells were then integrated to prioritize and evaluate FOS. A total of 502 DEGs and 54 intersected CAG-related genes were identified, with enrichment in wound healing, epithelial junction organization, tight junctions, cAMP signaling, gastric cancer, and digestive or secretory pathways. Five key genes-APOA1, CFTR, FOS, HMOX1, and VIM-were identified, all with AUCs above 0.80. Among 21,679 single cells, FOS was the only key gene predominantly enriched in gastric epithelial cells. Virtual knockout predicted associations between FOS-network perturbation and five genes involved in hormone processing and gastric secretory pathways. Docking generated candidate fisetin-FOS and kaempferol-FOS poses for preliminary compound prioritization. MNNG reduced GES-1 cell viability and significantly increased FOS mRNA expression. Integrated computational analyses highlighted FOS as an epithelial-associated candidate gene in CAG and suggested exploratory associations with gastric secretory pathways. These findings support further functional and compound-intervention studies of the FOS/AP-1 axis.

title: Temporal and Cellular Organization of Immune Responses to Live Attenuated Herpes Zoster Vaccination.
abstract: Background: Cellular responses to live attenuated herpes zoster vaccination and their variation with age remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to define their temporal and cellular organization and identify immune features that differed between age groups. Methods: Using a nested cohort design, we evaluated conventional humoral and CD4 T cell responses in 100 adults at Day 0 and Day 30. Olink protein profiles were assessed in 50 participants at Day 0 and Day 1, and longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing was performed in 18 participants at Day 0, Day 1, and Day 30. Results: Vaccination increased gE and VZV antibody levels by Day 30, whereas CD4 T cell cytokine responses were more variable. Olink profiling identified broad early changes shared by both groups and exploratory differences in selected immune and inflammatory proteins. At single-cell resolution, the broadest transcriptional response occurred at Day 1, led mainly by classical monocytes and naive CD4 T cells, followed by a more selective state at Day 30. Differences between age groups involved baseline plasmacytoid dendritic cell abundance and non-classical monocyte regulatory activity, the early conventional dendritic cell type 2 response, and later CD8 T cell and regulatory programs. Conclusions: These findings connect conventional immunogenicity with proteomic and cellular responses and identify selected immune states and pathways that differed between age groups across response phases.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Virus Detection: From Metagenomic Discovery to Clinical Decision Support and Population Surveillance.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly central to modern virus detection, particularly as metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) expands diagnostic and surveillance capabilities beyond targeted assays. This paper reviews how AI supports virus detection across three interconnected levels. The metagenomic layer forms the technical core of the review, while the clinical and population sections examine how sequence-level AI outputs are translated into patient-level and public-health decision support. At the metagenomic level, AI addresses key bottlenecks caused by fragmented assemblies and weak homology signals. Foundation-model approaches such as ViraLM leverage pretrained genome representations to improve viral contig discrimination under short-contig conditions, whereas LucaProt integrates sequence- and structure-informed learning to detect highly divergent RNA viruses via RdRP (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase)-focused discovery. At the clinical level, targeted molecular tests remain effective when the suspected pathogen is known, while mNGS provides a complementary, hypothesis-free approach that can broaden etiological investigation in complex infections when laboratories apply appropriate quality control and clinicians interpret results in context. At the population level, early warning systems combine heterogeneous data sources (epidemiological, open-source, digital, environmental, and wastewater signals) with AI methods to enhance outbreak detection and forecasting. Across all levels, robust contamination control, transparent reporting, external validation, and standardized interpretation criteria determine real-world value. Overall, hybrid pipelines that integrate molecular evidence, clinical metadata, and population-scale surveillance within governed, reproducible workflows are likely to provide the greatest impact.

title: In Vivo CRISPR Screen Identifies RPS19 as an Immunotherapy Target in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Despite the remarkable clinical success of immunotherapy, its efficacy against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains severely limited, highlighting an urgent need for novel targets and strategies to overcome immune evasion. Here, we aimed to identify key regulators of HCC immunity via unbiased functional screening and develop a targeted therapy to remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We performed an in vivo CRISPR-knockout screen using a 4500-gene sgRNA library in syngeneic HCC mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing of human HCC tissues and in vivo macrophage-depletion assays were utilized to dissect cellular populations and validate underlying mechanisms. We identified ribosomal protein S19 (RPS19) as a central mediator of HCC immune evasion, whose deletion in HCC cells mitigates the immunosuppressive TME. Mechanistically, scRNA-seq pinpointed tumor-associated macrophages as the key effector subset, whereby complement C5a receptor 1 (C5aR1) transduces RPS19 signals to trigger macrophage-dependent immune suppression. We further constructed SP94-peptide-modified disulfide-bond-containing nanoparticles (SNPSS) for targeted CRISPR-Cas9 delivery. SNPSS efficiently homes to HCC cells, releases payloads within the glutathione-rich TME, downregulates RPS19, reverses immune suppression, and robustly suppresses HCC progression in vivo. Collectively, the RPS19-C5aR1-macrophage axis fuels HCC immune escape, and SNPSS-based RPS19 gene-editing offers a promising strategy to remodel the TME and boost HCC immunotherapy efficacy.

title: Integrative graph deep learning with directional decoding for robust gene regulatory network inference from single-cell transcriptomics.
abstract: While gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are fundamental to understanding complex cellular mechanisms, the accurate inference from single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is hindered by the inherent noise, transcriptional dropout events, and dynamic nature of gene regulation. Current computational approaches often overlook long-range regulatory interactions, lack explicit modeling of regulatory directionality, and suffer from limited generalizability. To address these limitations, we introduce scGRAIL, a supervised deep learning framework that combines inductive local-aware graph aggregation (LGA) with an asymmetric relation decoder to enable robust GRN inference. Within this framework, LGA performs multi-hop neighborhood aggregation on a transcription factor (TF)-target graph, jointly leveraging topological structure and gene expression to capture long-range regulatory dependencies. A node reconstruction autoencoder (NAE) imposes gene expression reconstruction constraints on the latent embeddings, thereby enhancing robustness to noise and data heterogeneity and improving generalization. An asymmetric difference mechanism is introduced during decoding for distinct modeling of TFs and target genes; by computing an ordered difference vector between their embeddings, the model explicitly captures the directionality and target specificity of TF-target regulatory interactions, facilitating more accurate identification of potential causal regulatory relationships. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the model's superiority: it achieves optimal performance on 86.4% of benchmark datasets (38/44), surpassing state-of-the-art methods. Notably, scGRAIL achieves a 4.25% increase in average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) across four real-world networks compared to the graph contrastive link prediction (GCLink) model, yielding a 17.64% AUROC improvement for the TF500+ Non-Specific network in the mouse hematopoietic stem cells with lymphoid-lineage (mHSC-L) dataset, demonstrating its resilience to noise and scalability for large-scale GRNs. These results establish scGRAIL as a transformative tool for uncovering gene regulatory logic in single-cell transcriptomics. Overall, scGRAIL enhances structural modeling and directional discrimination in single-cell GRN inference by using multi-hop graph aggregation to capture long-range regulatory dependencies, expression reconstruction constraints to improve cross-dataset robustness, and an asymmetric decoding mechanism to explicitly model the regulatory directionality between TFs and target genes.

title: Direction-aware graph attention modeling and co-expression integration reveal novel core regulators of shared drought and salinity stress responses in rice leaves.
abstract: Although differential expression analysis has identified numerous drought- and salinity-responsive genes in rice, it cannot resolve the directional, transcription factor (TF)-driven regulatory architecture underlying responses across independent drought and salinity datasets. To address this, we applied TF-Anchored Directed SiGaResNet, a signed, direction-aware graph attention residual network with a TF-anchored edge-retention rule and permutation-based validation, to RNA-seq profiles from 92 rice leaf samples (51 stress, 41 control) derived from independent drought and salinity studies. Unlike conventional correlation- or co-expression-based approaches, the framework constrains regulatory inference around TF nodes while learning directed, signed relationships through supervised graph representation learning. Differential expression analysis identified 719 genes (405 upregulated, 314 downregulated), with induced transcripts enriched in stress-response and hormone-signaling processes and repressed transcripts dominated by photosynthesis- and secondary-metabolism-related processes. The framework showed strong cross-validated classification performance (MCC = 0.78 ± 0.17; AUC = 0.95 ± 0.05). The resulting directed gene regulatory network comprised 137 nodes and 163 edges and exhibited a sparse, modular architecture (modularity = 0.77; 15 communities), with TFs significantly enriched among regulatory source nodes (P < 0.001). Hub regulators were distributed across multiple TF families, predominantly bZIP, MYB-related, and NAC. Eighteen of thirty-two prioritized TF-encoding genes were independently corroborated within stress-associated WGCNA modules, and four comparatively uncharacterized candidates (Os07g0176200, Os05g0569300, Os03g0231000, and Os02g0187700) received convergent computational support from promoter cis-element enrichment, protein functional-association topology, and leave-one-out cross-validation classification. Quantitative real-time PCR further confirmed stress-responsive expression of all four candidates under separate drought and salinity treatments, supporting their prioritization as putative candidate regulators. These findings indicate that direction- and sign-aware graph attention modeling can integrate transcriptomic information from independent drought and salinity studies to identify biologically coherent, TF-centered regulatory patterns and prioritize candidate regulators for further functional investigation, without establishing causal regulatory mechanisms.

title: Identification and characterization of a novel distinct Pineal Neoplasm with Neuroendocrine and Epithelial Differentiation (PINNED).
abstract: Pineal region tumors are rare neoplasms that occur in all ages and account for less than 1% of all central nervous system (CNS) tumors in adults but are more frequent in children. Here, we describe a previously unrecognized tumor type of pineal origin characterized by a unique and consistent DNA methylation profile that does not match any known CNS tumor class and is distinct from all currently recognized pineal tumor entities. The presented cohort (n = 27) displayed a balanced sex distribution with a mean patient age of 35 years (range 7-75 years). The histopathological analyses demonstrated a highly cellular tumor showing various degrees of necrosis, mitotic activity, papillary structures, rosettes, epithelioid cytology, or signet-ring cells. The tumors consistently expressed cytokeratin 18, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and OTX2, whereas CRX expression was absent. Four out of 16 tumors (25%) showed ATRX mutations and/or loss of protein expression as revealed by immunohistochemistry. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing confirmed molecular distinctiveness from other pineal neoplasms but revealed the closest similarities to papillary tumors of the pineal region (PTPR). Projection of the transcriptome data onto the cellular trajectory of the developing murine pineal gland suggests that pinealocyte progenitors are the cellular origins. Taken together, our findings define a novel type of pineal region tumor that we provisionally named 'Pineal Neoplasm with Neuroendocrine and Epithelial Differentiation' (PINNED). Recognition of this tumor type appears to be important for the accurate diagnosis of pineal region tumors and may have implications for future tumor classification and treatment strategies.

title: CQRM: A Composite Quantile Regression Model for Differential Expression Analysis of Non-Coding RNA Count Data.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) play important roles in various biological processes, primarily via regulating gene expression at multiple levels. Nevertheless, compared to protein-coding genes, ncRNAs are relatively understudied. They are characterized by low expression, large variation, and more dynamic expression across different tissues and cell types, which creates unique challenges in differential expression (DE) analysis. Methods: We propose the CQRM, an adaptive multi-quantile testing framework for ncRNA count data that incorporates jittering to accommodate discrete counts, combines dependent evidence across quantiles, and selects the most informative quantile subset for distinguishing conditions. Results: The CQRM captures diverse expression differences, including changes in variability, skewness, and modality beyond mean shifts. Model-based simulations showed that the CQRM improved the detection of differentially expressed ncRNAs while controlling the false discovery rate relative to existing DE tools, especially when DE genes exhibited multimodal expression patterns and counts were low. Critical ncRNAs and biologically interpretable targeted pathways were identified when we further applied our method to a Smart-seq-total single-cell RNA-seq dataset and a human organ developmental RNA-seq dataset. Conclusions: CQRM complements mean-based DE methods by capturing heterogeneous ncRNA expression changes, supporting the identification of candidate ncRNA biomarkers and regulatory processes relevant to development and disease.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Identify CCR2-Dependent Monocyte-Smooth Muscle Cell Crosstalk in Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: Aortic aneurysm (AA) involves inflammatory recruitment and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) remodeling, but the cellular contribution of candidate chemokine receptors remains unclear. We prioritized reproducible AA-associated genes, localized their cellular sources, and tested whether monocyte CCR2 influences human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs). Differentially expressed genes shared by GSE57691 and GSE7084 underwent enrichment, protein-protein interaction, regulatory-network, and drug-gene analyses. Hub genes were assessed in GSE9106 and localized in GSE166676 single-cell RNA-sequencing data. CCR2-silenced THP-1 monocytic cells were indirectly co-cultured with HASMCs. CCR2 knockdown was verified by quantitative PCR; HASMC remodeling-related proteins and 24-h scratch-wound closure were evaluated. We identified 107 common upregulated genes and ten immune-related hubs. CCR2 was monocyte-enriched and higher in AA cells overall (p = 0.00799) and AA monocytes (p = 0.00440). THP-1 co-culture increased COL3A1 and SPP1, decreased α-SMA and TPM, and increased HASMC wound closure. CCR2 silencing partially reversed these changes and decreased wound closure versus siNC-THP-1 cells (p < 0.01). Multi-omic evidence and non-contact co-culture support CCR2-dependent monocyte-HASMC paracrine crosstalk in AA-associated remodeling. The responsible mediators and in vivo relevance require further study.

title: Targeting MRPL37 disrupts the pro-tumorigenic mitochondrial cascade in bladder cancer: from LRPPRC deficiency to ROS/AKT axis inhibition.
abstract: Bladder cancer (BLCA) is a urinary system malignant tumor with high morbidity and mortality worldwide. There is an urgent need for new biomarkers and therapeutic targets. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing, MitoCarta database and the Cancer Genome Atlas data, this study found that mitochondrial ribosomal protein L37 (MRPL37) was significantly up-regulated in BLCA, and its expression level was related to disease progression and poor prognosis. Functional experiments in vitro and in vivo confirmed that knockdown of MRPL37 could inhibit the proliferation, invasion, migration, metabolism and cisplatin resistance of BLCA cells by cell experiments, mouse subcutaneous tumor model, mouse orthotopic bladder cancer model and patient-derived organoid (PDO) model. A novel MRPL37-LRPPRC-ROS-AKT signaling axis was identified: loss of MRPL37 leads to the disorder of branched-chain amino acid metabolism, down-regulates the key mitochondrial protein LRPPRC, and then causes mitochondrial membrane potential damage and reactive oxygen species accumulation, which ultimately exert anti-cancer effect by inhibiting the AKT pathway. This study not only advances the understanding of the mechanism by which mitochondrial translation defects drive tumorigenesis, but also highlights the potential of MRPL37 as a target in BLCA prognosis and targeted therapy.

title: Elevated GANAB fuels PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint-mediated immune escape by maintaining PD-L1 stability in bladder cancer.
abstract: Bladder cancer (BCa) is one of the most common malignancies of the urinary system, with limited treatment options and extremely poor prognosis in advanced stages. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have been approved for clinical use, the objective response rate remains low (15%-25%), and acquired resistance frequently develops. The molecular mechanisms underlying PD-L1-mediated immune evasion in bladder cancer remain incompletely understood. Post-translational modification of PD-L1, particularly N-glycosylation, stabilizes the protein and enhances its immunosuppressive function; however, the specific enzymes regulating this process have not been systematically identified in BCa. We analyzed single-cell sequencing data from public databases to identify malignant epithelial subpopulations and constructed prognostic models using high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA), LASSO regression, and machine learning. Crucially, we performed extensive experimental validation beyond bioinformatics prediction: Ganab was stably knocked down in MB49 bladder cancer cells using lentivirus-mediated shRNA, and the effects on cell proliferation and migration were assessed by CCK-8 and wound healing assays. An orthotopic bladder cancer model was established in C57BL/6 mice by intravesical inoculation of MB49-luciferase cells, with tumor growth monitored by live bioluminescence imaging. Tumor tissues were subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing to dissect the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) at single-cell resolution. Mechanistically, Western blotting, PNGase F deglycosylation, immunofluorescence, and bidirectional co-immunoprecipitation were employed to elucidate how GANAB regulates PD-L1 glycosylation. Flow cytometry and CellChat analysis were used to evaluate T-cell subset remodeling and PD-L1/PD-1 signaling attenuation. We identified a malignant epithelial subpopulation (Epi_3) characterized by high tumor stemness scores and extensive copy number variations. A 15-gene prognostic signature was successfully constructed, in which GANAB exhibited the highest predictive weight. GANAB protein expression progressively increased along the pseudotime trajectory of tumor progression. Experimentally, inhibition of Ganab significantly suppressed MB49 cell proliferation and migration in vitro, and markedly inhibited orthotopic tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, GANAB regulated PD-L1 N-glycosylation, yielding two distinct PD-L1 bands: a 45 kDa glycosylated form (Gly-PD-L1) and a 33 kDa non-glycosylated form (Non-gly-PD-L1). Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed that GANAB specifically interacted with non-glycosylated PD-L1 (33 kDa) but not with glycosylated PD-L1 (45 kDa), indicating that GANAB interacts with non-glycosylated PD-L1 and may facilitate its entry into the ER glycosylation pathway. Single-cell analysis of shGanab tumor tissues revealed profound remodeling of the TIME: exhausted T cells (Tex) were reduced, effector memory T cells (Tem) were increased, and PD-L1/PD-1 signaling between tumor cells and T-cell subsets was attenuated. SCENIC analysis identified Stat1 as a key upstream transcription factor, and IMvigor210 cohort analysis confirmed positive correlations among GANAB, STAT1, PD-L1, and CD8A expression. Patients with high GANAB expression exhibited poorer immunotherapeutic responses and worse prognosis. Our findings establish a robust prognostic model for BCa patients through integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptome analysis. More importantly, we demonstrate through both in vitro and in vivo experiments that the core gene GANAB promotes bladder cancer progression and immune evasion by regulating PD-L1 N-glycosylation along the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, thereby remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. In the TCGA cohort, GANAB expression correlated strongly with the T-cell-inflamed gene expression profile (TEP; Spearman R = 0.85, P < 2.2e-16), indicating that GANAB-high tumors represent an inflamed yet immunotherapy-resistant phenotype. We acknowledge that the relationship between GANAB and other established biomarkers, including tumor mutation burden and PD-L1 combined positive score, as well as its expression profile across normal tissues, remains to be characterized. Furthermore, specific GANAB inhibitors are currently unavailable, and the ubiquitous expression of GANAB as a housekeeping endoplasmic reticulum enzyme raises potential on-target safety concerns that preclude immediate therapeutic targeting. Therefore, rather than advocating direct GANAB inhibition, we propose that GANAB serves as a candidate stratification biomarker and mechanistic node for glycosylation-mediated checkpoint resistance. Its clinical utility should be evaluated alongside emerging modalities such as ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicines and antibody-drug conjugates, with future efforts focused on biomarker validation and the development of tumor-specific delivery strategies before any therapeutic application can be considered.

title: Development and External Validation of an M2 Macrophage-Related Prognostic Signature in Breast Cancer Using Multi-Omics Data and Machine Learning.
abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), particularly the M2-like phenotype, are central regulators of breast cancer progression; however, clinically applicable models capturing their functional heterogeneity and biological mechanisms remain limited. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk RNA-seq data to construct an M2 macrophage-centered gene landscape. A machine learning framework based on 10-fold cross-validation was used to develop a prognostic signature in the TCGA-BRCA cohort (training set), with external validation in the independent GSE96058 cohort. Immune infiltration, genomic instability, pathway activity, and cell-cell communication were analyzed. KLF4 was examined in breast cancer cells and macrophages using qRT-PCR, Western blotting, siRNA-mediated knockdown, and a Transwell co-culture system. We identified a 16-gene M2 macrophage-related signature (M2MMS) that stratified patients into subgroups with distinct survival outcomes in both cohorts. High-risk tumors showed M2 macrophage enrichment, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, elevated genomic instability, and activation of E2F and MYC proliferative programs. Cell-cell communication analysis identified MDK-NCL as a dominant tumor-TME signaling axis. KLF4 was upregulated in breast cancer cells and in macrophages after co-culture, and silencing KLF4 attenuated CD206 induction, indicating that KLF4 is functionally involved in tumor cell-induced M2-like polarization in vitro. The M2MMS links M2 macrophage-driven immune remodeling to breast cancer prognosis and provides a basis for risk stratification and mechanistic investigation. KLF4 represents a regulatory node in tumor-macrophage interaction in vitro; its role in vivo and the clinical utility of the M2MMS require further validation.
